text.p: Tatham Offshore Inc said Tuesday drilling on Garden Banks Block 117 has validated its estimates of initial proven reserves for the block but it is disappointed that the working interest owners have elected not to test the deeper horizons at this time.

It said Leviathan Gas Pipeline Partners LP's Flextrend Development Co LLC subsidiary has completed drilling operations on the Garden Banks Block 117 No. 2 well and related sidetrack well located on the block offshore Louisiana in the Gulf of Mexico. Flextrend and Occidental Petroleum Corp's MidCon Corp are the working interest owners.

After reviewing the initial logs from the GB 117 No. 2 well, the operator concluded that the target Glob alt "A" sand appeared to be faulted out and the working interest owners decided to conduct a sidetrack operation, Tatham said.

It said the sidetrack encountered about 48 feet of vertical pay in two reservoirs. Logs indicate the sidetrack well encountered about 18 feet of pay in the Glob alt "A" sand, the producing interval in the GB 117 No. 1 well, which is currently producing about 1,800 barrels of oil and 4.3 million cubic feet of natural gas per day.

The Garden Banks 117 acreage contains deeper exploratory promise. However, because of the additional time and expense involved in conducting the sidetrack well, the working interest partners have decided not to continue drilling operations for deeper prospective horizons, Tatham said.
It said Flextrend intends to set casing to the current depth of the well and place the Glob alt "A" sand on production as soon as possible.
Tatham Offshore has a 25 percent reversionary interest in the GB 117 project, after repayment of certain development financing. Deep Tech International Inc owns about 38 percent of Tatham Offshore.
"We are pleased that the GB 117 No. 2 sidetrack well has validated our estimates of initial proven reserves for Garden Banks Block 117," Tatham's statement said.

"We are, however disappointed that the working interest owners have elected not to test the deeper horizons at this time. Hopefully, a deeper well can be drilled next year to test the exploratory prospect offered by our 3-D seismic work."
